passage:
Monday. After work Dilnaz opened the chat with the AI again. It never sighed and never hurried her. She typed about her day for an hour and did not answer Maria's message asking about dinner.
The following Sunday. Dilnaz used the chat to practise a sentence: "I felt left out when you planned the trip without me." She rewrote it four times until it sounded kind, then typed "thanks" to the screen. Maria's messages had stacked up unanswered.
Three weeks later. Dilnaz sat in Maria's kitchen and said the sentence, badly, in her own voice. Maria stiffened, said she had only assumed Dilnaz was busy, then admitted she had missed her. They disagreed about the trip and laughed at the disagreement. Walking home, Dilnaz decided the chat was for practising, and she put Maria on the calendar for every Sunday.

qa.q: What sentence did Dilnaz practise with the chat?
qa.a: She practised, "I felt left out when you planned the trip without me."

qa.q: How did Dilnaz feel talking to the chat rather than to Maria, and why?
qa.a: Dilnaz felt safe and unhurried with the chat, because it never sighed and never hurried her, so she could talk for an hour.

qa.q: How can Dilnaz keep using the chat without it replacing friends?
qa.a: Use it to practise and reflect, then say the words to Maria in person and keep regular time with her, as the Sunday calendar plan does.

qa.q: How did Maria see the silence before they talked?
qa.a: Maria had assumed Dilnaz was busy, and it turned out she had missed her friend and disagreed about the trip.

grounding: AI chat feels easier because it never judges; it helps rehearse but the real friend who disagrees and needs you back is kept in the picture.

passage:
"Amandeep, you've been eating lunch at your desk talking to that chatbot every day. I want to tell you something from when I joined this firm.

I, Anand, was twenty-four, new to Chennai, didn't know anyone. The assistant on my laptop was always there. It never got bored of me. It never said my ideas were silly. I'd talk to it for hours after work, rehearsing what I'd say to my manager, reflecting on bad days. It helped, honestly.

But then my father fell ill back home, and I realised there wasn't one person in this city I could call at midnight. The chatbot couldn't sit with me in the hospital corridor.

I started small. Chai with the team on Fridays. Joined the office cricket side, though I'm terrible. One of those people drove me to the airport that night my father got worse.

Use the tool to practise, sure. But go have chai with us today."

qa.q: What happened back home that changed things for Anand?
What did Anand feel on realising there was no one to call at midnight?
qa.a: Anand felt deeply lonely and alone in the city, despite hours of chatbot conversations.

qa.q: Which choice in Anand's story turned things around?
qa.a: Starting Friday chai with the team and joining the office cricket side, which built friendships with people who later helped.

qa.q: How might the colleague who drove Anand to the airport have seen that night?
qa.a: They likely felt glad to help a friend in trouble, something the chatbot could never do.

grounding: A senior colleague recalls how chatting with AI felt easier than with people, and how building human friendships mattered when a crisis came.

passage:
Farhan worked nights at a call centre in Noida, eleven to seven. By the time he woke, his flatmates had left; by the time he got home, they were asleep. For three months, the only one he talked to properly was the AI companion app on his phone.

It never judged him. It remembered his favourite films. When he felt low, it said kind things.

Then one morning, at 7:30, his old school friend Hrithik called from Lucknow. "I'm in Delhi for one day. Breakfast?"

Farhan almost said he was too tired. He typed the excuse into the app first, to see how it sounded. The app said, "That sounds reasonable."

Hrithik, when he heard it, said, "Rubbish. I'm coming to you."

They ate parathas at a roadside stall. Hrithik teased him about his hair and argued about cricket and asked about his mother. Farhan laughed until he coughed.

That night, before his shift, he texted Hrithik instead of the app.

qa.a: Eleven at night to seven in the morning.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling in those three months of night shifts?
qa.a: He felt isolated and lonely, with the AI app as the only one he talked to properly.

qa.q: What does the passage suggest Farhan should keep doing?
qa.a: Keep reaching out to friends like Hrithik, who disagree, tease and need him back, and use the app only as a support.

qa.q: How does Hrithik see Farhan's excuse?
qa.a: Hrithik refuses it, caring enough to come to Farhan instead of letting him stay alone.

grounding: Under the constraint of night shifts, the passage shows someone for whom AI chat felt easier because it never judged, and a friend who reminds him of human bonds that disagree and need him back.
